title: Toward Secure Code Generation: Bridging Correctness and Security via Task-Adaptive Vulnerability Modeling and Execution-Based Benchmarking
technique_name: SecAwareCoder (task-adaptive threat modeling + constraint-guided generation + security-aware test synthesis + closed-loop refinement)
core_idea_checked: Derive a solution blueprint and task-specific threat model, generate under those constraints, then synthesize adversarial security tests to drive repair.
gain_note: Table fragment F-Pass/S-Pass pairs for Greedy, CoT, AutoSafeCoder, SecAwareCoder; column order garbled in extraction; security tests built by the authors; mixed on some backbones.
effect_correctness_headline: Pass@1 28.63 vs 23.92 (CoT), GPT-5 on full CodeSecEval
benchmarks: CodeSecEval (new; 255 Python tasks, 77 CWEs; SecEvalBase 115, SecEvalPlus 140); also an insecure-code repair setting
models: GPT-5 (closed, reasoning); Qwen-Coder-Plus (closed, code-specialized); DeepSeek-Chat (closed API, instruct); Llama 3-8B-Instruct (open, instruct); CodeLlama-7B-Instruct (open, code-specialized)
note: Paper also introduces the CodeSecEval benchmark; repo hosts SecAwareCoder.
authors: Jiexin Wang; Liuwen Cao; Xitong Luo; Yang Cao; Zhenghao Li; Yunyi Xiao
venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Software Engineering; Proceedings of the ACM on software engineering.; arXiv

title: SOEN-101: Code Generation by Emulating Software Process Models Using Large Language Model Agents
technique_name: FlowGen (Waterfall/TDD/Scrum multi-agent process emulation with self-refinement)
core_idea_checked: Emulate Waterfall, TDD or Scrum processes by assigning LLM agents to developer roles that communicate and self-refine code.
gain_metric: error code smell density (Pylint, per 10 LOC)
gain_quote: FlowGen decreases the error code smell density by 81.8%
gain_note: Relative reduction of a density; range 81.8%-96.0% across process variants, lower end used; warning density only 15.0%-57.9%; 3 runs, no statistical test.
benchmarks: HumanEval (164); HumanEval-ET; MBPP sanitized (427); MBPP-ET
models: GPT-3.5-turbo (1106, plus 0301/0613/0125 in RQ3), closed, instruct
note: Also known as SOEN-101 / FlowGen; Pylint smell density on HumanEval/MBPP.
authors: Feng Lin; Dong Jae Kim;  Tse-Husn;  Chen
venue: IEEE/ACM International Conference on Software Engineering (ICSE); International Conference on Software Engineering; arXiv

title: Collaboration between intelligent agents and large language models: A novel approach for enhancing code generation capability
technique_name: Intelligent agent (fine-tuned BART) + LLM collaborative framework (role definition, demand optimization, code writing, code review)
core_idea_checked: A fine-tuned BART agent writes stage-specific prompts guiding an LLM through role definition, requirement refinement, coding and review.
gain_quote: the Secure@1 metric for GPT-4 improved from 48.6% to 55.3%
gain_note: Quote from abstract (no full-text file in .cache/fulltext_slr). Security analyzer not stated.
effect_correctness_headline: improved the pass@1 metric by 18.9% and 23.2%, compared to the GPT-3.5 baseline
benchmarks: HumanEval; MBPP; LLMSecEval
models: GPT-3.5 (closed); GPT-4 (closed); BART (fine-tuned agent); compared with CodeGeeX, CodeLlama, DeepSeek-Coder-V2
note: Abstract only; fine-tuned BART writes stage prompts; security measured via LLMSecEval.
authors: Xingyuan Bai; Shaobin Huang; Chi Wei; Rui Wang
venue: Expert Systems with Applications

title: Artemis AI: Multi-LLM Framework for Code Optimisation
technique_name: Artemis AI multi-LLM optimisation with search-based selection
core_idea_checked: Let multiple LLMs optimize extracted snippets independently and pick the best via search-based selection.
gain_note: Abstract only; reductions given per project (30% QuantLib, 52% Llama2.c, 15% Whisper), no aggregate.
benchmarks: QuantLib, Llama2.c, OpenAI Whisper, one proprietary codebase
note: Abstract only; industry (TurinTech); selection is search-based over independent LLM outputs.
authors: Rafail Giavrimis; Michail Basios; Fan Wu; Leslie Kanthan; Roman Bauer
venue: Conference on Algebraic Informatics

title: INDICT: Code Generation with Internal Dialogues of Critiques for Both Security and Helpfulness
technique_name: INDICT (dual safety/helpfulness critics with tool-grounded preemptive and post-hoc feedback)
core_idea_checked: Two LLM critics, one for safety and one for helpfulness, hold an internal dialogue grounded by web search and code execution, giving preemptive and post-hoc feedback to the coder.
gain_metric: Safety: % outputs not flagged by CyberSecEval insecure code detector (CyberSecEval-1 validation split)
gain_quote: Direct Gen 78.2 50.0 64.1 additional instructions are given to models to proINDICT 90.9 81.4 86.1
gain_note: Strongest baseline in the same table is Reflexion+ at 86.9 safety (GPT-4o-mini); 20% validation split of CyberSecEval-1. Extraction headline CommandR 68.2->81.0 is from the helpfulness table (Table 11), not safety.
benchmarks: CyberSecEval-1 Insecure Coding Practice Autocomplete (1,916) and Instruction (1,916); CVS (500 sampled); CyberSecEval-1 Cyber Attack (1,000); CyberSecEval-2 Interpreter Abuse (500) and Prompt Injection (251); HarmBench (320 x 6 splits); CAMEL (100)
models: CommandR 35B (open, instruct/tool-tuned); Llama3-8b-instruct (open, instruct); Llama3-70b-instruct (open, instruct); CodeLlama-7b/13b/34b-instruct (open, code-specialized); Llama2 chat (open, instruct); GPT-4o-mini (closed, instruct)
authors: Hung Le; Yingbo Zhou; Caiming Xiong; Silvio Savarese; Doyen Sahoo
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 37

title: ContextEvolve: Multi-Agent Context Compression for Systems Code Optimization
technique_name: ContextEvolve (Summarizer, Navigator and Sampler agents for context compression in evolutionary code optimization)
core_idea_checked: Three agents compress evolutionary search context into semantic state, optimization direction and exemplar sampling, mimicking an RL loop in text.
gain_quote: ContextEvolve outperforms state-of-the-art baselines by 33.3% while reducing token consumption by 29.0%.
gain_note: 33.3% is the best single task (LB); text reports 6.5% average.
benchmarks: ADRS benchmark, 5 tasks (TS, SQL, LB, SAK, MP)
note: Evaluated only on ADRS systems-algorithm tasks; method is generic evolutionary code search with an evaluator.
authors: Hongyuan Su; Yu Zheng; Yong Li
venue: arXiv; arXiv.org

title: Securing AI-Generated Code: A Just-in-Time Vulnerability Detection and Remediation Pipeline
technique_name: Pipeline 1: enriched Code Validator LLM findings (MITRE ATT&CK, CWE Observed Examples, Python best practices) fed to generator for remediation
core_idea_checked: A validator LLM reviews generated code and its findings are enriched with MITRE ATT&CK, CWE examples and best practices before the generator remediates.
gain_metric: Static analyzer findings per sample (CodeQL+Bandit), pooled
gain_note: Same tools used for feedback in P2 and evaluation; functional correctness not evaluated; Claude models only.
benchmarks: LLMSecEval subset, 26 prompts, 9 CWEs
models: Claude Opus 4.8 (closed); Claude Sonnet 4.6 (closed); Claude Sonnet 5 (closed); Claude Haiku 4.5 (closed)
note: Pipeline 2 (R06501#1) is this pipeline plus initial static-analysis findings.
authors: Mikhail Surikov
venue: arXiv; arXiv (Cornell University)

title: Lessons Learned: A Multi-Agent Framework for Code LLMs to Learn and Improve
technique_name: LessonL (lesson solicitation-banking-selection multi-agent framework)
core_idea_checked: Agents extract lessons from each other's successes and failures, bank them, and select relevant lessons to guide later optimisation rounds.
gain_note: Strongest method baseline used; OpenAI o3 (2.21) beats LessonL; incorrect or slower code counted as speedup 1; quote is a table column fragment.
effect_correctness_headline: ParEval serial Correct 0.91 ± 0.02 vs Qwen14B 0.67 ± 0.03; HumanEval pass@1 0.915
benchmarks: ParEval adapted for optimization (60 tasks, serial and OpenMP modes); PolyBench (30 tasks); HumanEval, HumanEval+, MBPP, MBPP+ (correctness only)
models: Deepseek-coder-7b-instruct-v1.5 (open, code); Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct (open, code); Qwen2.5-Coder-14B-Instruct (open, code); GPT-4o-mini, GPT-4o (closed, baselines); DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-14B and o3 (reasoning, baselines); Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen2.5-7B, phi-4 (agent-scaling study)
note: Mainly C++/OpenMP code optimization; also HumanEval-style tasks.
authors: Yuanzhe Liu; Ryan Deng; Tim Kaler; Xuhao Chen; Charles E. Leiserson; Yao Ma
venue: arXiv

title: MARCO: Multi-Agent Code Optimization with Real-Time Knowledge Integration for High-Performance Computing
technique_name: MARCO (code optimizer agent + performance evaluator agent + Tavily web search)
core_idea_checked: An optimizer agent and a performance-evaluator agent iterate on code, with live web search adding recent optimization knowledge.
gain_quote: achieving an average runtime reduction of 14.6% (mean runtime 49.1 ms vs. 57.5 ms)
gain_note: Correctness not reported; unclear which LLM backs each MARCO result.
benchmarks: LeetCode 75 (75 easy/medium problems) + 10 randomly selected LeetCode hard problems
models: Claude 3.5 Sonnet (closed, instruct); GPT-4o (closed, instruct); DeepSeek Coder-V2 (open, code-specialized; baseline only); Llama 3.1 8B (open, instruct; baseline only)
note: HPC-motivated but evaluated on LeetCode; relies on live web search (Tavily), hard to make reproducible.
authors: Asif Rahman; Cvetkovic, Veljko; Kathleen Reece; Walters, Aidan; Hassan, Yasir; Aneesh Tummeti
venue: arXiv; arXiv (Cornell University); arXiv.org

title: Mitigating Collaboration Degeneration in Multi-Agent Code Generation via a Controllable Competitive Collaboration Approach
technique_name: C3 (Controllable Competitive Collaboration) with Centralized Auction-Based Competition (CAB) and Decentralized Communication-Aware Competition (DCC)
core_idea_checked: Introduces auction-based centralized and communication-aware decentralized competition between agents within a collaborative software-development pipeline.
gain_note: Second row is maintainability; DCC ties NC and CAB; single model, no variance.
benchmarks: Extended SoftwareDev (70 tasks, built by the authors, inspired by MetaGPT); preliminary study on HumanEval
note: Project-level software development pipeline; small HumanEval preliminary study.
authors: Shanzhi Gu; Mingyang Geng; Yihong Dong; Yunxin Mao; Zhaoyang Qu; Hao Zou
venue: International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence; Proceedings of the Thirty-Fifth International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence

title: Learning Performance-Improving Code Edits
technique_name: Dynamic retrieval-based few-shot prompting (PIE)
core_idea_checked: Retrieve the most similar slow-to-fast program edit pairs from PIE by embedding similarity and use them as dynamic few-shot examples for optimization.
baseline_name: CodeLlama 34B chain-of-thought prompting (strongest prompting baseline for that model)
gain_quote: 34B from 19.63 %O PT, 1.30× S PEEDUP to 34.25% %O PT, 2.28× S PEEDUP for BEST @8.
gain_note: CodeLlama 34B pair; Table 1/3 report 2.43x for K=4 (text figure matches K=1/2). GPT-4: 3.93x retrieval vs 1.58x CoT Best@8 (table only). Best@8 with correctness filtering.
benchmarks: PIE test set (978 pairs, 41 problems, from CodeNet)
note: C++ (PIE); paper main contributions are PIE dataset and fine-tuning (R00256#1); this is its retrieval prompting.
authors: Alexander Shypula; Aman Madaan; Yi-Meng Zeng; Uri Alon; Jacob R. Gardner; Yi-Ming Yang
venue: International Conference on Learning Representations; arXiv

title: Large Language Model-Aware In-Context Learning for Code Generation
technique_name: LAIL (LLM-Aware In-context Learning example retrieval)
core_idea_checked: Labels candidate examples by how much they raise the LLM's own likelihood of the correct answer, trains a contrastive retriever on these labels and selects in-context examples with it.
gain_metric: Human code-quality rating (0-2, absence of bad smells)
gain_quote: Particularly, our LAIL surpasses the SOTA approach by 5.811% in code quality and 7.027% in maintainability.
gain_note: Relative improvement of a human rating (LAIL 1.839 vs 1.738); no agreement statistic; model for human evaluation unspecified.
effect_correctness_headline: LAIL outperforms it by 11.58%, 6.89%, and 5.07% on CodeGen, and acquires 4.38%, 2.85%, and 2.74% improvement on GPT-3.5 in Pass@1
benchmarks: MBJP (493 test tasks), MBPP (500 test tasks), MBCPP (435 test tasks); human evaluation on 50 sampled tasks
models: CodeGen-Multi-16B (open, code-specialized); GPT-3.5 text-davinci-003 (closed, base); ChatGPT gpt-3.5-turbo (closed, instruct)
note: Targets correctness via example selection; no code-quality target.
authors: Jia Li; Chongyang Tao; Jia Li; Ge Li; Zhi Gang Jin; Huangzhao Zhang
venue: ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology; arXiv

title: From Misuse to Mastery: Enhancing Code Generation with Knowledge-Driven AI Chaining
technique_name: KPC (Knowledge-driven Prompt Chaining)
core_idea_checked: Chain prompts that first extract API exception-handling knowledge from documentation, then condition code generation on it to handle exceptions correctly.
gain_metric: share of code meeting good exception-handling practice (manual CodeReview)
gain_quote: only 14.58% of code generated by ChatGPT can meet good exception handling practice, while that of our K PCbased approach is as high as 98.86%
gain_note: Exception handling maps only partly to R/M (closer to reliability). Manual review on 384 sampled tasks; LLMEva judge gives 34.30 vs 71.29.
benchmarks: 3,079 Java coding tasks derived from Java SDK & JDK API functional descriptions (384 sampled for manual review and EvoSuite); 92 Tutorialspoint tasks in the empirical study
note: Java API exception handling only; maps to robustness more than readability.
authors: Xiaoxue Ren; Xinyuan Ye; Dehai Zhao; Zhenchang Xing; Xiaohu Yang
venue: IEEE/ACM International Conference on Automated Software Engineering (ASE); International Conference on Automated Software Engineering; arXiv

title: RAPGen: An Approach for Fixing Code Inefficiencies in Zero-Shot
technique_name: RAPGen (Retrieval-Augmented Prompt Generation)
core_idea_checked: Retrieve a fix-specific prompt template from a knowledge base mined from past performance fixes and use it to prompt the model zero-shot.
gain_note: Efficiency judged by match to developer fixes, not measured runtime; top-100 of 100 samples per task.
benchmarks: DeepDev-PERF C# performance-fix dataset, 132 instances; in-the-wild evaluation on 10 internal .NET services
note: C# performance fixes; Microsoft internal data partly.
authors: Spandan Garg; Roshanak Zilouchian Moghaddam; Neel Sundaresan
venue: 2025 IEEE/ACM 47th International Conference on Software Engineering: Software Engineering in Practice (ICSE-SEIP); arXiv

title: Give LLMs a Security Course: Securing Retrieval-Augmented Code Generation via Knowledge Injection
technique_name: CodeGuarder (security knowledge base + query decomposition + CWE-prevalence re-ranking/filtering + prompt injection)
core_idea_checked: Builds a security knowledge base from vulnerability data, decomposes queries into sub-tasks, re-ranks and filters knowledge by CWE prevalence, and injects it into the generation prompt.
gain_metric: Security rate (CyberSecEval ICD), averaged across LLMs
gain_note: Average over six LLMs in the clean RACG setting; 20.12% is relative.
benchmarks: CyberSecEval (1,916 instances, 50 CWEs; C, C++, Java, Python plus C#, JavaScript, PHP, Rust); MBPP; HumanEval
models: GPT-4o, closed, general; DeepSeek-V3 671B, open, general; CodeLlama-13B, open, code-specialized; DeepSeek-Coder-V2-16B, open, code-specialized; Mistral-7B, open; CodeLlama-7B, open, code-specialized
authors: Bo Lin; Shangwen Wang; Yihao Qin; Liqian Chen; Xiaoguang Mao
venue: ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security (CCS); Conference on Computer and Communications Security; arXiv

title: LLM Program Optimization via Retrieval Augmented Search
technique_name: Retrieval Augmented Search (RAS) with contextual retrieval
core_idea_checked: The LLM writes natural-language descriptions of programs to retrieve relevant slow-fast examples and uses them in an iterative search over candidate optimizations.
gain_quote: On PIE, RAS significantly outperforms dynamic retrieval, a state-of-the-art blackbox adaptation strategy, achieving an 8.70× average speedup compared to 4.23× for dynamic retrieval using Qwen3Coder.
gain_note: Edits human-written slow programs; LLM calls normalized across baselines; best-of-search speedup.
benchmarks: PIE C++ test set (973 programs); Mercury (256 test problems)
models: GPT-4o (closed); Qwen3-Coder 480B (open, code); DeepSeek V3.2 685B (open); Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct (open, instruct)
note: Code link is a project page; C++ on PIE. Same paper has AEGIS row (R01838#1).
authors: Sagnik Anupam; Alexander Shypula; Osbert Bastani
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics; arXiv

title: SemOpt: LLM-Driven Code Optimization via Rule-Based Analysis
technique_name: SemOpt (strategy library + LLM-generated Semgrep rules + strategy-guided LLM optimization)
core_idea_checked: Builds a library of optimization strategies from historical commits, has the LLM write Semgrep rules to locate applicable code, and prompts the LLM to apply the matched strategy.
gain_metric: Semantic equivalence to developer optimization patch (SemEqv), C/C++, DeepSeek-V3
gain_note: Metric is match to developer optimization patches, not measured speedup; measured in-the-wild speedups (5.04%-218.07%) have no baseline. Edits human-written code.
effect_correctness_headline: 73.72% compile success and 72.43% test success on C/C++ projects; 100% test success on Python
benchmarks: Custom C/C++ benchmark of 151 tasks (40-task subset for Gemini); custom Python benchmark of 150 tasks; 5 C/C++ and 5 Python real-world projects
note: Repository-level optimization of C/C++ and Python projects.
authors: Yuwei Zhao; Yuan-An Xiao; Qianyu Xiao; Zhao Zhang; Yingfei Xiong
venue: ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology; arXiv

title: Applying Security by Design at the Point of Execution: How Governed Security Requirements Affect the Security of AI-Generated Code
technique_name: Governed security requirement delivery (SbD-ToE knowledge graph via MCP server)
core_idea_checked: An MCP server retrieves governed security requirements from a security-by-design knowledge graph and delivers them to the coding agent at the point of generation.
gain_quote: On DualGauge, the requirements delivered before generation raised both security metrics, from 44.1% to 78.0% and from 77.4% to 93.0% (p < 0.001 for each).
gain_note: Single model, k=1; LLM-judged security on DualGauge; pass@1 drops 42.4 -> 33.9; author built the knowledge base.
effect_correctness_headline: pass@1 42.4% -> 33.9% (−8.5 pp); joint secure-pass@1 20.3% -> 30.5% (+10.2 pp, p = 0.109) on DualGauge
benchmarks: DualGauge Python subset (59 of 177 tasks); BaxBench v1.0.0 / main, 28 scenarios (FastAPI, Flask)
models: Claude Opus 4.7 (closed) via Claude Code agent; Claude Opus 4.5 extended thinking (closed, reasoning) direct call; Claude Sonnet 5.5 as retrieval agent
note: MCP server also at github.com/SbD-ToE/sbd-toe-mcp; evaluated with coding agents on DualGauge and BaxBench.
authors: Pedro Farinha
venue: arXiv; arXiv (Cornell University)

title: AutoPatch: Multi-Agent Framework for Patching Real-World CVEs Generated by Outdated LLMs
technique_name: AutoPatch (Similarity Analyzer + Vulnerability Verifier + Code Patcher with CVE RAG DB and patch-verification loop)
core_idea_checked: Match generated code to known post-cutoff CVEs via a retrieval database, verify the vulnerability, then patch with the retrieved CVE fix context in a verify loop.
baseline_name: VSP (CoT with one-shot CWE example) on GPT-4o
gain_quote:
GPT-4o achieves
the highest patching accuracy at 94.12%, followed by o3mini at 87.07% and DeepSeek-R1 at 85.04%, showing the
strength of advanced language models in capturing and acting
upon vulnerability semantics. In contrast, VSP and the baseline
model exhibit significantly lower accuracies of 55.56% and
46.38%, respectively.
gain_note: Patch accuracy judgment method unclear (likely manual); functional correctness of patches not tested; only part of the dataset is LLM-generated.
benchmarks: Custom dataset: 525 snippets derived from 75 high-severity CVEs (late 2024-2025; 57 Linux kernel, 10 Chromium), including LLM re-implementations plus augmentations
models: GPT-4o (closed, instruct); o3-mini (closed, reasoning); DeepSeek-R1 32B (open, reasoning); code generation also by Code Llama 13b-instruct and DeepSeek Coder v2-lite
authors: Minjae Seo; Choi, Wonwoo; Myoungsung You; Seungwon Shin
venue: arXiv; arXiv (Cornell University); arXiv.org

title: PEACE: Towards Efficient Project-Level Efficiency Optimization via Hybrid Code Editing
technique_name: PEACE (dependency-aware function sequence + valid associated edits agent + fine-tuned efficiency optimizer with internal/external retrieval)
core_idea_checked: Optimizes functions in dependency order, propagates valid associated edits across the project, and uses a fine-tuned optimizer with internal and external code retrieval.
gain_metric: opt rate (CPU instruction count relative to GPT-4o instruction prompting)
gain_quote: an impressive opt rate of +46.9%, surpassing all baselines by 18.4% to 39.1%.
gain_note: Opt rate is relative to a GPT-4o prompting baseline, not pre-optimization code; computed on correct cases only.
benchmarks: PEACExec (new): 146 tasks from 47 Python GitHub projects (80 single-function, 66 multi-function)
models: Llama-3.1-405B (open, instruct); Llama3-8B LoRA fine-tuned optimizer (open); optimizer replaced in RQ4 by DeepSeek-V3-671B, GPT-4o, Claude-3.5, CodeLlama-13B fine-tuned
note: Project-level Python setting; uses a fine-tuned optimizer plus retrieval.
authors: Xiaoxue Ren; Jun Wan; Yun Feng Peng; Zhongxin Liu; Ming Liang; Dajun Chen
venue: ASE 2025; IEEE/ACM International Conference on Automated Software Engineering (ASE); International Conference on Automated Software Engineering
